cohort: 98 pairs of twins delivered at a gestational age of 32 weeks and above
finding: There were no differences in maternal postpartum complications or neonatal outcomes between vaginal and cesarean delivery groups, but vaginal delivery was associated with a longer inter-twin delivery time interval, less estimated blood loss, and shorter maternal hospital stay.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a longer inter-twin delivery time interval, less estimated blood loss, and shorter maternal hospital stay compared to cesarean delivery.
